answer: A progressive Sybil fee can choke fake identities: every new account linked by payment trail, device fingerprint, or timing pattern pays a fee that rises steeply with each sibling identity, so the marginal cost of the tenth fake dwarfs the first. Honest newcomers pay only a small base fee, refunded after clean trading. Picture a dune field: crossing one dune is cheap, but an attacker marching an army over ridge after ridge faces a growing delta in cost at each step, and the umber ledger marks clusters that try to split fees across proxies, letting the market throttle them together.
